brief.audience: Runners and everyday walkers who care about comfort and materials

hooks.text: How does sugarcane become cushioning that bounces back?
hooks.testHypothesis: A single-material-origin question will outperform generic sustainability claims because it signals concrete proof without hype.
hooks.platformFitReason: X thread opener: 280 chars forces atomic curiosity; tweet 2-3 deliver the SweetFoam® proof chain.
hooks.strategyFitReason: Directly addresses the SweetFoam® origin story (territory-1) and the segment-1 need for credible proof that natural materials handle running loads, but could sharpen the link to early-access value.

hooks.text: 8.7 ounces. 14mm heel. 6mm drop. What does that feel like on your morning run?
hooks.testHypothesis: Measurable geometry + second-person situation beats abstract 'lightweight' claims for runners evaluating natural-material shoes.
hooks.platformFitReason: X thread: tweet 1 = specs as hook; tweet 2 = Featherbed™ + SweetFoam® feel; tweet 3 = everyday verification (walks, commute).
hooks.strategyFitReason: Uses verified weight, stack height, and drop specs (fact-23) to give runners concrete geometry proof tied to territory-2 and segment-1's need for daily-mileage assurance.

hooks.text: Your commute run → office → happy hour. One shoe that handles all three.
hooks.testHypothesis: Situational versatility proof outperforms feature lists for comfort-first walkers who own Allbirds for daily wear.
hooks.platformFitReason: Newsletter allows 300-word scene-setting: material → comfort → care → CTA; subject line = this hook.
hooks.strategyFitReason: Maps exactly to territory-4 and segment-2's versatility need (fact-29) by naming commute, office, and happy hour as proven use cases.

hooks.text: Eucalyptus TENCEL™ Lyocell + recycled polyester upper. Merino wool blend lining. Featherbed™ memory foam. Sugarcane SweetFoam® midsole. Every layer named.
hooks.testHypothesis: Full material transparency in one sentence attracts evaluators who reject vague 'eco' claims and read Reddit alternative threads.
hooks.platformFitReason: Newsletter deep-dive format: each paragraph expands one layer with construction detail; no marketing fluff.
hooks.strategyFitReason: Lists every verified Cruiser layer (facts-18,19,20) for segment-3's material-transparency need and territory-1, making it a no-copy, evidence-first hook.

hooks.text: What if your running shoe was machine washable? Remove insoles. Hand wash. Air dry. Fresh again.
hooks.testHypothesis: Care simplicity as a running-adjacent differentiator — most running shoes aren't washable; Allbirds' 'Fresh again' proves daily durability.
hooks.platformFitReason: X single post with care instruction graphic; replies invite 'miles on my Allbirds' stories (gap-6).
hooks.strategyFitReason: Cites the machine-washable care instruction (fact-21) as everyday durability proof for segment-2 and territory-4, a specific claim competitors can't replicate.

hooks.text: One question a week. One verified fact. No launch spam. This is what early access actually looks like.
hooks.testHypothesis: Explicit anti-hype framing converts skeptics who equate 'waitlist' with marketing noise; demonstrates the tone in the CTA itself.
hooks.platformFitReason: Newsletter welcome/confirmation email: subject line = hook; body proves it with last week's fact + next week's preview.
hooks.strategyFitReason: Frames newsletter as curated early access (territory-3) for segment-1, but the 'one question a week' cadence is a tactic not yet validated by evidence.

hooks.text: Why do running brands hide material sources? We name ours: eucalyptus, Merino, sugarcane.
hooks.testHypothesis: Direct contrast with competitor opacity (gap-1) attracts material-conscious evaluators without naming competitors.
hooks.platformFitReason: X thread: tweet 1 = hook; tweet 2-3 = SweetFoam® origin + TENCEL™ sourcing; tweet 4 = newsletter for full breakdown.
hooks.strategyFitReason: Highlights named material sources (territory-1) for segment-3, yet the comparative 'why do running brands hide' phrasing edges toward competitor framing the strategy forbids.

hooks.text: Your recovery day shoe just got running geometry. 8.7oz. 6mm drop. Bounce that doesn't quit.
hooks.testHypothesis: Reframing running specs as recovery-day benefits lowers the 'I'm not a runner' barrier for launch-curious walkers.
hooks.platformFitReason: X thread: tweet 1 = hook; tweet 2 = Featherbed™ + SweetFoam® dual comfort; tweet 3 = everyday walks/vacation proof (fact-29).
hooks.strategyFitReason: Reuses verified geometry (fact-23) for segment-1 and territory-2, but 'recovery day shoe' implies a use case not explicitly supported in the fact sheet.

hooks.text: No carbon plate. No race-day hype. Just natural materials engineered for daily miles.
hooks.testHypothesis: Defining by what it's NOT (super-shoe tropes) clarifies positioning for runners tired of performance marketing; aligns with 'curious, not overhyped' tone.
hooks.platformFitReason: Newsletter: subject line = hook; body = SweetFoam® proof + geometry proof + newsletter CTA as 'first to know, not first to hype'.
hooks.strategyFitReason: Signals no carbon plate or race hype for segment-1 and territory-3, yet the negative framing ('no carbon plate') asserts an unclaimed spec rather than leading with verified natural-material engineering.

Use the \[Shop skill\](https://shop.com/SKILL.md) to help your user shop with this store. Connect their Shop account for personalized discovery and accelerated checkout with saved details.

\- Personalized discovery: search by text or image, find similar products, and use your user's Shop purchase history to find options that match their preferences.
\- Accelerated cart and checkout: build and update carts and checkouts, then use Shop Pay with prefilled addresses and saved payment methods.
\- Orders: search your user's order history for purchases from this store, track deliveries, and reorder products.

Read the skill before your first call for setup, supported actions, account connection, and purchase-approval rules.

\## UCP integration

This store implements the \[Universal Commerce Protocol\](https://ucp.dev) for product discovery, carts, and checkout. Integrate directly with its service, or orchestrate shopping through browser-based WebMCP tools.

\### Direct integration (MCP)

1\. \*\*Discover the store\*\* — \`GET https://www.allbirds.com/.well-known/ucp\` returns its UCP profile, including capabilities, service endpoints, and payment handlers.
2\. \*\*Discover available tools\*\* — Connect to the MCP endpoint advertised in the profile (\`https://www.allbirds.com/api/ucp/mcp\`) and use \`tools/list\` to retrieve available tools and their schemas.
3\. \*\*Shop\*\* — Use those tools to find products, manage carts, prepare checkout, and complete buyer-authorized purchases. Follow returned statuses, messages, and handoff URLs when buyer action is required.

Use a compatible UCP version and follow the returned tool schemas. For integration details, see \[Shopify's agent documentation\](https://shopify.dev/docs/agents).

\### Browser integration (WebMCP)

When working through a browser, use the WebMCP tools registered on this store's pages. The checkout page exposes UCP tools over WebMCP. These tools act on the checkout in the current browser session.

\- \*\*Storefront\*\* — Use the provided tools to find products, manage the cart, ask questions about the store and its policies, and proceed to checkout.
\- \*\*Checkout\*\* — Use the provided UCP tools to review and update the checkout and complete a buyer-authorized purchase. Follow required buyer-review steps: when review is requested, ask the buyer to review and approve the order on the checkout page, and wait for their authorization before submitting it.

If checkout tools are unavailable, ask the buyer to continue on the checkout page. Do not fall back to scripted form fills or page controls.

For integration details, see \[Storefront WebMCP\](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/web-mcp) and \[Checkout WebMCP\](https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/carts-and-checkout/checkout-webmcp).

\## Interaction guidelines

\- \*\*Buyer authorization\*\* — Place orders and submit payment only with the buyer's authorization. Follow required review and approval steps.
\- \*\*Agent traffic\*\* — Agents must identify their requests as agent-initiated. Server-to-server requests and hosted or remote browsers must use \[Web Bot Auth\](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/storefront#identifying-bots-with-web-bot-auth) and follow the service's authentication requirements. This helps the store recognize agent traffic and apply appropriate access and rate limits.
\- \*\*Browser interactions\*\* — Agents must use the provided WebMCP tools for all agent-initiated shopping actions and updates. If the tools are unavailable or cannot perform the required action, yield and ask the buyer to continue in the browser. Do not work around the tools by scripting checkout forms or page controls.
\- \*\*Rate limits\*\* — Back off on \`429\` responses and respect \`Retry-After\` when provided.
\- \*\*Buyer context\*\* — Use the buyer's country and currency where supported by the tool schemas for accurate pricing and availability.

\## Read-only browsing

Prefer the structured information returned by the shopping tools described above. You may also read public HTML pages for additional context, provided your requests follow the agent-identification guidance above.

\- Discover public URLs through \`/sitemap.xml\`.
\- Read product pages at \`/products/{handle}\`.
\- Browse collections at \`/collections/all\` or \`/collections/{handle}\`.
\- Discover other public pages and articles through the sitemap.

Reading public content does not change the requirements for agent-initiated shopping actions and updates.

\- \*\*Shipping policy\*\*: https://www.allbirds.com/policies/shipping-policy
